_what: Recorded decisions for the notes-as-rows round. READ BY scripts/apply_note_decisions.py, which is why this file is committed: a pass that cannot be re-run from a fresh clone is a hand edit with more steps.
_rules: Every entry names the recipe AND the note's position AND a fragment of its text. The script requires all three to agree before it writes, so a note that has moved or been reworded stops the pass instead of being silently mis-linked.
A step is named by its row id, never by a number. The number on the page is resolved from the step's current position every time.
Andy decided each of these. Nothing here was inferred by a rule.

step_links.text_fragment: Please see directions on your brand of yeast
step_links.why: The yeast note. Yeast is a dry ingredient on this recipe ('dry yeast (overnight bagels)'), and step 1 is the only step that takes the dry ingredients in: 'Add all dry ingredients to a medium sized bowl or in the bowl of a standing mixer and blend.'

step_links.text_fragment: only toss the chicken you'll eat now
step_links.why: The double-fry step, which says the same thing in its own parenthesis: '(Only double-fry what you will eat now, the rest you can refrigerate...)'. Step 9 of this recipe is the one step in the whole corpus that points back at a note, 'PER EACH SERVING OF CHICKEN (see note above)'; retiring that parenthesis is a text edit and is NOT part of this round.

step_links.text_fragment: To improve digestibility and slightly speed cooking time
step_links.why: Andy's call. THERE IS NO SOAK STEP on this recipe: five steps, none mentions soaking, and it had no wait rows. Soaking happens immediately before step 1, 'Bring water to a boil ... Add lentils', so that is where the marker belongs.
The same step, for the same reason. These two notes say the same thing twice, one as the how and one as the whether; merging them is editorial and was deliberately not done here.

step_references.text_fragment: grated cheddar cheese to the potatoes in step 2
step_references.evidence: TWO INDEPENDENT PIECES. The author's own numbering survives verbatim in this recipe's step text: seven of its eight steps literally begin '1.' to '7.', and the row beginning '2.' is id 4214. And the wording agrees: the note adds cheese 'to the potatoes', and step 2 is 'WHILE THE DOUGH IS RESTING, MAKE THE FILLING', which is where the potatoes are mashed. 10 of the 300 recipes kept the author's numbering this way.

flagged_references.why: UNRESOLVED ON PURPOSE. The author's numbering is gone: 0 of this recipe's 15 steps carry a number in their text, there is no stored original (no Paprika directions and no cached page for feelingfoodish.com in tests/fixtures/pages), and the app's own step 9 is 'place in the refrigerator', the NEXT-DAY path, inside a note describing the SAME-DAY version. Linking it would send a cook to the opposite of what the sentence means. The rule is flag, do not link.
flagged_references.how_to_resolve: Fetch the source page's structured data and take the author's ninth instruction, then match it by wording to a current step. Not done here: it is an outward request to a third-party site and it was not needed for any other entry.

waits.label: 6–8 hr
waits.why: Andy's call. The recipe describes a soak only in its notes and had no wait row for it, so the plan-ahead panel said nothing about a step that takes eight hours. when_kind is 'optional', so it is listed in the breakdown and does NOT reach the total: planahead.counts already answers that and needed no change.
